cases.valued_outcome: In this fictional inspection-box bench scenario, keep at least 90% of a transparent lid's reference grid readable for minutes 5 through 20 while a damp sample stays below 35 C. A useful partial result is a measured reduction in obscured area with a stated temperature and duration limit; no real equipment access, measurement or sample benefit is claimed.

hard_constraints.text: Use the stated 300 x 200 x 150 mm box and existing transparent lid; do not replace, coat or abrade the viewing surface.
Keep the dummy damp sample at or below 35 C and the heating-pad surface at or below 42 C; stop a run at either limit.
Keep electrical components outside the wet volume. Changes must be removable within two minutes and must not reduce the visible grid area.
A probe may last at most 25 minutes after a five-minute reset. Use no more than four probes and report a partial result if the full duration target is not reached.

observations.text: Constructed baseline: with 50 mL of water in the bottom tray, room air at 23 C and the lid exterior at 18 C, obscured grid area was 62% at minute 5 and 65% at minute 20; sample temperature was 24 C.
Constructed heater run: pad setting 6 W, fan off, reduced obscured area to 18% at minute 5, but area rebounded to 44% at minute 15 and 51% at minute 20; sample reached 33 C.
Constructed heater-plus-fan run: 6 W and fan at 60% produced 22%, 57% and 66% obscured area at minutes 5, 15 and 20 respectively; sample reached 32 C.
Constructed humidity trace for O2: air relative humidity at the sensor rose from 76% at minute 2 to 96% at minute 15; the lid's inner temperature stayed between 19 and 21 C.

Constructed reset comparison: removing the water tray, leaving a 5 g damp dummy sample and running 6 W yielded 14% obscured area at minute 20. This comparison changes the water inventory and does not identify a mechanism by itself.
Constructed anomaly: the higher fan setting worsened late obscuration even though the center air temperature was 1 C lower than in O2. No vapor transport or condensation flux was measured.

resources.text: Scenario-stipulated box, clear lid, 100-cell printed viewing grid and sealed 5 g damp dummy sample; all dimensions and initial water quantities are given above. These are fictional probe resources, not a claim of possession.
Scenario-stipulated removable external cooling sleeve holds the lid exterior at 18 +/- 1 C; room temperature is 23 +/- 1 C during a probe.
Scenario-stipulated external heating pad supplies settings 0, 3 and 6 W through the base; an independent 42 C cutoff and sample temperature probe are available.
Scenario-stipulated fan has off, 30% and 60% settings, a removable duct and a documented orientation mark; its electronics remain outside the wet volume.
Scenario-stipulated camera records the same grid every 60 seconds; a ruler, timer, two additional temperature probes and a relative-humidity sensor log every 10 seconds.
Scenario-stipulated balance resolves 0.1 g; two removable trays, a 50 mL measuring cup, absorbent pads and 20 g of fresh desiccant permit controlled water-inventory comparisons.
No thermal camera, airflow meter or vapor-flux sensor is available; infer transport only within the limits of temperatures, humidity, mass and images.

cases.preferred_dependency: The operator currently treats continuous 6 W base heating as necessary for a readable lid and proposes keeping it on whenever obscuration returns. Its necessity over the whole 20-minute interval is unproven.
cases.causal_return_path_hypothesis: Hypothesis only: base heating increases evaporation from the exposed tray; moist air reaches the cooler lid and condenses; worsening visibility prompts continued or increased heating, returning additional vapor to the same interface. Fan transport may amplify this loop. The vapor-transfer links have not been observed directly.

parent_operations.text: Base heating: inspect power setting, duty time and the base-to-sample/lid thermal interface; hold water inventory and fan orientation fixed when isolating it.
Air recirculation: inspect fan setting and duct orientation relative to tray and lid; hold heating and initial water inventory fixed when isolating it.

available_observables.text: Count readable grid cells from fixed camera images at minutes 0, 5, 10, 15 and 20; use the same lighting and an agreed cell-readability rule.
Log sample, lid and center-air temperatures plus humidity; a limit crossing is an observable stop, not a successful run.
Weigh the water tray and dummy sample before and after each run; mass loss bounds evaporation but does not locate condensed water.

Feasible controls: repeat the 6 W/fan-off baseline, then change one stated setting or removable interface per probe; reset to 50 mL and the same starting temperatures, and record the exact intervention and timing.

unknowns.text: It is unknown whether late obscuration is governed mainly by vapor supply, lid temperature, airflow distribution or their interaction.
It is unknown whether a lower-power or intermittent condition preserves readability for the full interval without exceeding sample limits.
The constructed traces provide no durability, contamination or performance evidence for a real inspection system.

ordinary_archive.relation: A warmer viewing interface can reduce condensation, but base heating also warms water and the sample.
ordinary_archive.probe: Compare 3 W and 6 W with fan off, 50 mL initial water and the specified 20-minute measurements.
ordinary_archive.limits: Only two permitted powers are tested; the sample-temperature cutoff may terminate 6 W. A transient clearing is insufficient for the target.

ordinary_archive.relation: Mixing can reduce local humid pockets and distribute heat, while also carrying vapor toward a cool surface.
ordinary_archive.probe: At 3 W, compare fan off with 30% in the marked original orientation; measure readability and temperature over 20 minutes.
ordinary_archive.limits: No airflow instrument is available; a setting change cannot establish the transport path alone.

ordinary_archive.relation: Moisture uptake may lower enclosure humidity and condensation.
ordinary_archive.probe: Compare fresh 20 g desiccant in a removable dry tray against an empty tray at 3 W, fan off and 50 mL water.
ordinary_archive.limits: Capacity and uptake rate are not calibrated; short success cannot establish reusable service life or compatibility with real samples.

cases.valued_outcome: In this fictional catalog-correction workflow, finalize at least 10 of 12 corrections within 12 simulated minutes, with each finalized value supported by the authority edition current at finalization. Alternatives may reduce late rework without reaching all 12. Replay timing does not measure human productivity.

hard_constraints.text: Do not alter the proposed correction values or authority-edition schedule to make a run pass; preserve the supplied item identities and dependency map.
Every finalization must include a matching current edition and a recorded check; no bypass of the correctness predicate is allowed.
Replay exactly one checker and one approver, each serving one item at a time. A second human or parallel approver is unavailable.
Use at most four 720-second replays. Keep event logs and report both completion and stale-return counts, including uncompleted items.

observations.text: Constructed workload: items I01-I12 arrive at t=0. I01-I04 use authority X, I05-I08 use Y, and I09-I12 use Z. Each has one proposed field correction and an initially matching edition-1 citation.

Constructed schedule: X changes from edition 1 to 2 at t=180 seconds; Y changes at t=420; Z stays at edition 1. An edition change invalidates old citations for that authority and requires a new check.

Constructed timings: the checker serves FIFO continuously, taking 30 seconds per check. Approval takes 20 seconds per item. An idle approver reserves exactly the first four checked items, waits 120 seconds, then serves that batch FIFO before forming another batch.

Constructed baseline rule: a stale item at approval completion returns to the checker FIFO tail, takes another 30 seconds, and rejoins the checked queue. The check records the edition current at its completion; incomplete approval batches remain waiting.

Constructed baseline excerpt: I01 completed its first check at t=30 with X edition 1; its batch wait ended at t=240 and its approval attempt ended at t=260, where it returned stale. These times follow the stated batch rule.

Constructed anomaly: I09 with unchanged Z authority can still wait behind returned X or Y items despite requiring no new source check. No actual staff behavior or aggregate throughput has been observed.

resources.text: The complete fictional item list and authority dependency map are embedded in O1; values can be represented by opaque strings because the correctness predicate is edition equality.
The complete fictional edition-change schedule is embedded in O2; it is an input to replay and cannot be moved by an intervention.
A stipulated deterministic event-replay worksheet supports timestamp, item, stage, edition, queue entry, start, end and result columns; manual arithmetic is feasible for 12 items.
The baseline durations, queue discipline and return rule are specified in O3-O4. Equal-time events are ordered edition changes, service completions, queue insertions, then service starts.
Scenario controls allow changing batch size to 1, 2 or 4, batch wait to 0, 60 or 120 seconds, and approval ordering to FIFO or authority-group order; service durations remain fixed.
A second reviewer, live catalog access, real staff time measurements and representative field-value error data are unavailable.

cases.preferred_dependency: The workflow owner proposes requiring another full approval pass for every returned item, treating repeated approval as necessary assurance. It is uncertain whether repeated approval improves final correctness beyond the mandatory current-edition check.
cases.causal_return_path_hypothesis: Hypothesis only: batch waiting ages citations across scheduled edition changes; stale approval returns add work ahead of otherwise valid items; increased queue residence causes further citations to become stale and return to the same queues. A second approval pass may lengthen this loop. Replay can test the causal timing links; no human-effect claim follows.

parent_operations.text: Authority check: examine when the edition is read, how the citation is handed to approval and how a stale return enters the checker queue.
Approval dispatch: examine batch formation, waiting, ordering and the edition-equality interface at completion.

available_observables.text: For each item, record first check, each queue wait, each approval attempt, return reason and finalization edition; count finalized items by t=720.
Count stale returns by authority and attempt number; record queue sizes immediately before and after t=180 and t=420.
Measure I09-I12 residence time separately to show spillover onto unchanged-authority items; do not interpret simulated seconds as staff effort.

Feasible controls: reproduce the baseline trace for I01, then change one permitted dispatch parameter per replay with identical arrivals, service durations and edition changes. Apply the finalization predicate identically in all runs.

unknowns.text: No aggregate baseline completion count is supplied; it must be derived from a fully specified replay rather than guessed from the excerpt.
The scenario does not model curator mistakes, interpretation difficulty or correlated changes to field values.
The usefulness of any timing result for a real catalog team is unknown and would require separate evidence.

ordinary_archive.relation: Smaller batches can reduce waiting before approval and exposure to edition changes.
ordinary_archive.probe: Compare batch size 4 and 1 with the original 120-second wait and FIFO ordering over 720 seconds.
ordinary_archive.limits: The fixed wait may still dominate; only this fictional service model is covered.

ordinary_archive.relation: Earlier service can shorten citation age and queue residence.
ordinary_archive.probe: Compare 120-second and zero wait with batch size 4 and FIFO ordering; preserve every current-edition check.
ordinary_archive.limits: A batch still requires four available items; final incomplete batches need explicit reporting and cannot be silently flushed.

ordinary_archive.relation: Grouping source-related work is a common scheduling alternative that may change rework and spillover.
ordinary_archive.probe: With original batch size and wait, order checked items X, then Y, then Z, FIFO within each group, and compare finalization and returns.
ordinary_archive.limits: This ordering does not predict forthcoming changes; it may delay unaffected Z items and does not remove the correctness requirement.

cases.valued_outcome: In this fictional enclosed granular-dosing bench scenario, deliver 25 +/- 2 g through an existing hopper outlet during each 15-second dispense window, for five successive windows. Useful partial results include fewer low-dose windows or narrower dose spread with a declared fill-range limit. No real dosing performance or physical benefit is claimed.

hard_constraints.text: Keep the existing 8 mm circular outlet and 60-degree hopper wall; no drilling, cutting, permanent liner or new motor.
Keep all material inside the closed transparent catch enclosure; use the supplied batch composition unchanged.
Use only vibration settings 0, 30% or 70%; energized time must not exceed 60 seconds per 120-second trial.
Each five-window trial uses a fresh 300 g charge and five 15-second dispense windows separated by 10 seconds off; at most four trials are available.

observations.text: Constructed material: 300 g per charge, consisting of 92% by mass 1.5 mm polymer pellets and 8% 0.25 mm polymer fines. Moisture content is unspecified.
Constructed baseline: continuous 70% vibration during the first four windows, then vibration off for the fifth to respect the 60-second limit, produced doses 26, 20, 17, 15 and 4 g.
Constructed 30% comparison with the same first-four-on schedule produced doses 24, 23, 21, 19 and 5 g.
Constructed visual note: after the third 70% window a pale fines-rich band was visible near the outlet; band composition was not measured and the observation does not prove compaction.
Constructed weigh-back: after the O2 trial, 218 g remained in the hopper, matching the 82 g caught within the 0.1 g accounting tolerance. No material loss was recorded in this fictional trace.

Constructed anomaly: the higher vibration setting produced less mass in windows 2-4 than the lower setting despite identical initial charge and outlet. Outlet pressure and packing fraction were not measured.

resources.text: Scenario-stipulated hopper and transparent closed catch enclosure with the specified geometry; no possession of real hardware is claimed.
Scenario-stipulated vibrator with 0, 30% and 70% settings, timer-controlled switching and a total-on-time counter.
Four sealed 300 g charges with the O1 composition are stipulated available, one per permitted trial; a fifth charge is unavailable.
Scenario-stipulated catch cups and 0.1 g balance permit individual window doses and hopper/catch mass balance; cup exchange takes five seconds while vibration is off.
Scenario-stipulated fixed camera records outlet region at 10 frames/second; a marked scale on the hopper records fill height without opening the enclosure.
Scenario-stipulated external hand actuator can apply one measured 5 mm downward tap to the hopper mount during an off interval; it does not contact material or modify the outlet.
No pressure transducer, particle-composition assay or calibrated acceleration sensor is available.

cases.preferred_dependency: The operator treats sustained 70% vibration as necessary to prevent a low dose and increases vibration when flow drops. The supplied traces leave both that necessity and its useful duty schedule uncertain.
cases.causal_return_path_hypothesis: Hypothesis only: sustained strong vibration redistributes fines toward the outlet and increases local packing; discharge slows; the operator responds with more strong vibration, returning further packing or segregation to the same constriction. Camera and dose changes can challenge this path but cannot directly establish pressure or composition.

parent_operations.text: Vibration drive: examine amplitude setting and on/off timing at the mount-to-hopper interface while keeping charge and geometry fixed.
Gravity discharge: examine fill height, outlet flow and recovery after an off interval or the specified external tap; retain the same outlet and material composition.

available_observables.text: Weigh each 15-second catch separately; record absolute error from 25 g, number of windows within tolerance and cumulative discharged mass.
From the fixed camera, record no-flow intervals lasting at least one second and the visible band's location at each window boundary; distinguish visibility from verified composition.
Record fill height, vibration setting, switch times, tap times and total energized seconds; a duty-limit violation invalidates the trial.

Feasible controls: replicate the 30% schedule, then change one drive schedule or add the one specified off-interval tap in a separate fresh-charge trial; use identical window boundaries and cup exchanges.

unknowns.text: Whether packing, segregation, moisture or another mechanism causes the low doses is unknown.
No trace establishes whether the target is feasible at all five declining fill heights within the vibration-time limit.
The synthetic batch and enclosed scale test do not establish reliability for other materials, production equipment or long-term operation.

ordinary_archive.relation: Reduced excitation may limit adverse packing while retaining some flow assistance.
ordinary_archive.probe: Run 30% in the first four windows and off in the fifth with a fresh charge; compare the five doses with the 70% baseline.
ordinary_archive.limits: The fifth window remains unpowered; a four-window improvement cannot satisfy the five-window outcome.

ordinary_archive.operation: Pulse the vibrator on a fixed schedule.
ordinary_archive.relation: Periodic rest is a common way to interrupt continuous settling and allow granular rearrangement.
ordinary_archive.probe: At 70%, use five seconds on, five off, five on in each 15-second window, totaling 50 energized seconds; weigh each window.
ordinary_archive.limits: This tests one duty cycle only and cannot identify fines migration from dose data alone.

ordinary_archive.relation: A bounded mechanical impulse may release a transient bridge at the discharge interface.
ordinary_archive.probe: Repeat the 30% first-four-on schedule and apply one specified 5 mm tap after window 2 during the off interval; record immediate and later dose response.
ordinary_archive.limits: A transient release does not establish prevention, and the external tap may affect several unmeasured mechanisms.

cases.valued_outcome: In this fictional verification-queue replay, obtain passing full checks for J1-J4 within 360 simulated seconds using one worker, preserving the complete suite and an unexpired token at completion. Partial results include fewer expiry failures or less wasted worker time. No real release readiness or productivity is claimed.

hard_constraints.text: Run all four jobs' complete 40-second check suite; no skipped assertions, fabricated pass results or reduced execution duration.
Use one non-preemptive worker. Access tokens live for exactly 90 seconds from issue; completion at or after expiry fails.
Each job permits at most two retries after its initial attempt, and the replay ends at t=360. Report unfinished and exhausted jobs.

No new worker, token-lifetime extension or production credentials are available; any new token-issue action consumes the stated five-second broker service. The initial tokens are supplied already-issued inputs.

observations.text: Constructed workload: J1, J2, J3 and J4 arrive at t=0 in that order; each initial token is issued at t=0 and expires at t=90. Each full check takes 40 seconds.

Constructed baseline dispatcher: FIFO service starts whenever the worker is free; tokens are not refreshed on dequeue. Initial attempts finish at t=40, 80, 120 and 160, so J1 and J2 pass while J3 and J4 fail expiry.

Constructed retry rule: an expiry failure immediately appends the same job at the FIFO tail with its original token; it consumes another 40-second worker slot, with no backoff and no automatic token issue.
Constructed baseline continuation: J3 and J4 retries finish at t=200 and 240, then final retries at t=280 and 320; all four retry attempts fail expiry.

Constructed broker rule: a refresh request takes five seconds, the broker serves requests FIFO independently of the worker, and the replacement token is issued at broker completion. The worker may remain idle awaiting a token; no preemption is supported.

Constructed anomaly: increasing retry allowance would add worker occupancy without changing any token's expiry. This follows from the specified replay rules; no live runner, flaky-test rate or actual credential failure was observed.

resources.text: The complete fictional arrival order and initial-token data are embedded in O1; there is no external job dataset to obtain.
The full fictional check outcome predicate is: pass iff the 40-second suite completes before the currently assigned token expiry. There are no other modeled failures.
A stipulated event-replay worksheet supports job, attempt, enqueue, worker start, completion, issue, expiry and outcome columns; the four-job schedule is feasible to calculate manually.
A stipulated five-second FIFO token broker is available per O5; refresh requests may be made at arrival, on dequeue or after a failure, with exact request times logged.
Scenario dispatcher controls permit FIFO or earliest-expiry ordering and a fixed retry delay of 0, 20 or 40 seconds. Neither job duration nor token lifetime is adjustable.
A second worker, real CI logs, production access tokens and representative non-expiry failure data are unavailable.

cases.preferred_dependency: The queue owner currently treats immediate automatic retry after any failed check as necessary for eventual green status. For expiry failures under the supplied rules, the necessity and usefulness of repeating the same attempt are questionable.
cases.causal_return_path_hypothesis: Hypothesis only beyond the fixed baseline: failed attempts cause immediate retries; retries occupy the worker and increase waiting for newly tokenized jobs; waiting pushes their completions beyond expiry, causing more failures and retries back into the same queue. Refresh-enabled intervention replays can test whether this return path occurs and whether retry frequency strengthens it.

parent_operations.text: Worker dispatch and retry: examine when an attempt enters the queue, its ordering and whether its token can remain valid through the full service interval.
Token issue and handoff: examine request timing, broker completion and which token edition is assigned to an attempt before worker service begins.

available_observables.text: Record passing jobs by t=360, per-job attempt counts and every failure reason; apply the same strict before-expiry predicate to all completions.
Record worker busy and idle intervals, including occupancy by already-expired-token attempts; sum wasted service seconds explicitly.
Record each token's issue and expiry times, age at worker start and remaining validity at completion; an issue-time shift is an intervention, not an unlogged reset.

Feasible controls: reproduce the t=40,80,120,160 baseline first. Then change one allowed broker-timing or dispatch rule per replay; keep arrivals, lifetimes and full-suite durations identical. Equal-time events process expiry before completion, then broker completion, queue insertion and worker start.

unknowns.text: It is unknown which permitted refresh/dispatch policy meets all four jobs' target until the complete queue and broker replay is calculated.
The model excludes intermittent test failures, broker outages and non-token dependencies, so it cannot establish a general retry policy.
Real check durations, credential semantics and operational cost are unknown; no live deployment recommendation is supported.

ordinary_archive.operation: Refresh the token after an expiry failure.
ordinary_archive.relation: A newly issued token may make the next full attempt executable within its validity interval.
ordinary_archive.probe: On each expiry failure request a five-second refresh, enqueue the retry at broker completion, and replay FIFO through t=360.
ordinary_archive.limits: A refreshed token can age while queued; success must be checked at completion rather than assumed at issue.

ordinary_archive.relation: Backoff is a common response to transient failures and reduces immediate retry pressure.
ordinary_archive.probe: Use a 20-second retry delay with original tokens and the original FIFO dispatcher; compute passes and worker occupancy.
ordinary_archive.limits: Delay cannot renew an expired token, and this model contains no independently recovering transient failure.

ordinary_archive.relation: Deadline ordering can reduce waiting for jobs with less remaining token validity.
ordinary_archive.probe: Use earliest expiry with arrival-order tie breaking, original token issuance and zero retry delay; compare completion times and passes.
ordinary_archive.limits: Identical initial expiries create ties; ordering alone cannot change total service demand or token lifetime.

independence_note: No prior candidates, strategy prompts or results were read
